M1_never_serves_from_cache._note: Kills the READ half: every request goes to the network even when the object is stored. The feature's entire point.
M1_never_serves_from_cache.from:
const hit = await cache.get(ref);
    if (hit !== null) return hit;

M2_never_stores._note: Kills the WRITE half: nothing is ever cached, so the second read still costs a request. Reds WIDER than the read-half mutant on purpose: with nothing stored the two LRU axes (A10/A11) count entries in an empty store, so they red too. Named rather than narrowed.
M2_never_stores.to:
const resp = await inner(req);
    return resp;

M3_blob_integrity_by_declared_sha_only._note: Downgrades the blob check to the server's own `sha` field — exactly the weaker check that a tampered `content` with an intact `sha` walks through.
M3_blob_integrity_by_declared_sha_only.from:

M4_corrupt_entry_falls_back_to_network._note: Turns the fail-LOUD corruption path into fail-open. The sync would then silently re-fetch instead of reporting the damaged store.

M5_commit_sha_mismatch_accepted._note: Drops the commits/trees integrity check — an entry filed under the wrong sha would be applied.

M6_io_read_failure_becomes_fatal._note: Removes the fail-OPEN on an unreadable store: an EIO would abort the sync instead of falling through to the network.
M6_io_read_failure_becomes_fatal.to: let raw: string | null = await this.io.read(ref.key);

M7_eviction_order_is_most_recent_first._note: Inverts the LRU comparator — the freshly used entry would be evicted and the stale one kept.

M8_no_eviction_at_all._note: Removes the ceiling: the store grows without bound. A9 reds alongside A10 because the early return is the SAME statement both the direct-evict axis and the through-transport axis reach.

M9_mutable_refs_become_cacheable._note: Narrows the allow-list instead of widening it. ⛔ The obvious mutant — adding `refs` — reds NOTHING: `git/refs/heads/main` has an extra path segment, so the shape check refuses it before the type is read (double cover, stated in the source). Removing `blobs` is the reachable mutation of the same guard. A11 (the no-eviction control) reds too: with blobs excluded the store holds two entries instead of three, and that control counts them. Named rather than narrowed.

M10_ref_addressed_reads_admitted._note: Drops the hex-SHA gate, so `git/trees/main` (a MUTABLE read) would be cached — and path traversal would stop being structurally impossible. A13 (the through-transport twin) does NOT red under this single mutation and that is correct: `git/trees/main` would be admitted, but the integrity check then refuses to STORE a payload whose `sha` is not `main`, so the second read still goes out. A13 is held by two guards; A16 pins this one directly.

M11_non_get_requests_cached._note: Type-PRESERVING: `req.method === "NEVER"` does not compile (TS2367 — the union has no such member) and the driver reports BROKEN, which is the absence of a measurement, not one. Narrowing the guard to PATCH lets a POST through the cache path instead.

M12_query_variant_ignored._note: Collapses `?recursive=1` and the plain tree into one key — two DIFFERENT payloads under one entry.

M13_repo_dropped_from_key._note: Keys by SHA alone, so a private repo's object could be served for a different repository. Reds wide because the key is load-bearing for the fixtures too: A5-A7 tamper with a specific stored key, which no longer exists once the repo is dropped. Named rather than narrowed — a key change IS supposed to be visible.

M14_segment_class_relaxed._note: Owner/repo become anything at all. A19 drives the forms that SURVIVE `new URL`'s dot-segment normalisation (`..%00`, `..;`, `%252e%252e`) — those are the ones this class actually refuses.

M15_dot_segment_guard_removed._note: ⛔ Expected to red NOTHING, and that is the POINT: `new URL` normalises `.`/`..` away before any segment is read (A20 measures exactly this), so the guard is DEFENSIVE — it exists for a future parser swap. Kept in the matrix so the next reader sees the zero was measured, not overlooked.

M16_sweep_only_by_per_process_counter._note: Restores the reviewed defect: the LRU sweep gated solely on a per-PROCESS byte counter. Every CLI run builds a fresh cache, so a small delta would never sweep and the device-wide store would grow past its advertised ceiling across runs.

M17_stored_digest_not_checked._note: Drops the type-independent integrity layer. A tampered TREE body (A23) has no other guard — `?recursive=1` is a flattened listing whose hash is not recomputable — so it would be applied, and diffTrees would fetch the wrong blob for that path.
